differences.what: a pale stone band along the foot of the south wall (y 712-726 px), the wall's water table or a low coping before it; the build's front band (y about 731 px through this camera) returns about 0.5 m round the corner and stops
differences.how: T-2781: a course on the wall, not a coping: the brick runs on below it in the same plane to the fence and it throws a line of shadow along its underside. Built as K01's side belt (form.side_belts) in the trim limestone, 2.3-2.5 m and 0.05 m proud, along the whole south wall and stopped against the bay and the rear range: through this camera at y 712-725 px from the corner to the bay's base, against the photograph's 712-726. Its foot is the line the camera was fitted to, so this photograph places it in the wall and does not measure its height; at the corner it stands 0.07 m over the wing's string course, a corner no picture shows after the remodel (L-k01-1637-south-flank-2781)

differences.what: an ornate stone-dressed projection on the south wall from x 322 px (about u 3.9-5.2 m) to past the frame's edge: its front through the principal storey in tall round-arched lights between columns under a bracketed entablature, small round lights in its base (y 690-730 px), and on its top a balcony behind a balustrade (y 355-420 px)
differences.how: T-2780: the 1911 sheet's canted bay (s20fp-1637-b1, its junctions at x 1427.06 and 1430.61 m in the trace frame, so u 4.34 to 0.79, 0.75 m out on 45-degree cheeks) built on the south wall as a K08 canted bay in dressed stone: a base to 2.95 m with a small round-headed light under the front's principal light, a principal storey to 8.0 m with the front's round-arched light (1.35 m wide, 3.15-5.65 m), a bracketed entablature (consoles 0.6 m under a soffit 0.35 m out and a 0.25 m fascia to 8.25 m) and on its flat top a stone balustrade 0.7 m high round all three faces. Through this camera the bay's west junction lands at x 338 px against the photograph's 322-340, its balustrade's coping at about y 345 against 345, and its entablature at y 385-410 against 385-435. What of it is not yet built is listed below for T-2781

differences.what: the projection's columns: a column at each corner of the bay and between its lights, from the sill band to the capitals under the entablature (x 350-362 and 395-405 px, y 505-690)
differences.how: T-2781: engaged stone columns 0.2 m across on the bay (bays[south_flank].columns), at each front angle on its bisector and on each cheek 0.3 m from the wall, from the base's string course at 3.03 m to 6.15 m, each on a square base 0.15 m tall under a square capital 0.2 m tall: through this camera the cheek's column at x 351-362 px and the angle's at x 391-402, against the photograph's 350-362 and 395-405, from y 690 to the capitals at 505-520 against 505-515. The capitals stand plain, as square blocks; their carving is the dress item below

differences.what: the projection's carved dress: the oval lights or medallions in the frieze over the arches (y 470-500), the capitals' band (y 505-515), the consoles' scrolls and the corona's mouldings
differences.how: the entablature's consoles and fascia stand where the photograph's do (T-2780), plain, and the columns' capitals (T-2781) stand as plain square blocks under the band; the frieze's ovals, the capitals' carving, the arches over the lights, the consoles' scrolls and the corona's mouldings are T-2887's

differences.what: the cheeks' lights: a round-arched light in the west cheek between its columns (x 362-398 px, y 515-680) over a small light in its base (y 690-730), and the east cheek's, out of the frame, by symmetry
differences.how: T-2886: a round-arched light in each cheek between its two columns, 0.65 m along the 1.002 m cheek from the wall, 0.38 m clear from the sill band at 3.15 m to 5.8 m under a 0.05 m band (K06's head band named per window, so the light fits between the shafts), its recess the kit's 0.33 m minimum so it clears the front's; under it a round-headed light 0.3 by 0.55 m from 2.2 m. Through this camera the west cheek's glass lands at x 365-384 px against the photograph's 373-397, its crown at about y 527 against 517-520, and the base light at x 367-382, y 700-730 against 367-383, 693-723. The light stands about 8 px left with the cheek's angle column: the photograph's cheek is longer than the sheet's (the plan item below), so its width and place are the sheet's cheek's and not yet the photograph's (L-k01-1637-cheek-lights-2886)

differences.what: the front's round-arched light stands about 15-20 px left of the photograph's (x 406-436 px against 420-458) and its base light with it
differences.how: T-2886 weighed it: across the light at y 640 the photograph's glass is dark from x 421 to 447 px with stone from 448 to the crop's edge, so the light is about as wide as built and its centre about 9 px east of the sheet's front's centre. The light and the base light under it now stand 1.355 m along the 2.22 m front, 0.245 m east of its centre, as far as the east angle's column leaves room, under a 0.1 m band: through this camera the glass's east edge lands at x 447 against 447, its arch's west edge about 6 px left of the photograph's. What is left is the bay's plan, not the light: between the same two columns the photograph's west cheek spans about 47 px against the build's 37, and its angle column stands at x 398-408 against 389-397, so the photographed bay is larger than the 1911 sheet's (longer cheeks or a deeper projection). T-2887 weighs a deeper bay against the sheet (L-k01-1637-cheek-lights-2886)

differences.what: the window over the bay's open shutters (x 352-375 and 425-445 px)
differences.how: not built: K06 carries no shutter; T-2887's dress

differences.what: a second-storey window over the projection's balcony (x 350-445 px, y 305-355), round-headed between open shutters, the balcony's door or window
differences.how: T-2780: a round-headed light cut in the south wall over the bay's balustrade (K08 window_over), 1.4 m wide and 1.4 m tall on a sill at 8.4 m, so its crown stands at 9.8 m: through this camera its arch tops out at about y 300 px against the photograph's 305, between x 845 and 885 of the render (x 361-401) against the photograph's opening at about x 375-425. Its shutters are dress, open below

differences.what: a tall panelled stack with a corbelled cap rising behind the eave (x 245-345 px, its cap's top at y 30): on the south wall's line it stands at about u 6.0, its top about 14.2 m over grade
differences.how: T-2781: the photograph's ray through the stack's middle (x 295 px) and the engraving's through its drawn stack (x 690) meet in plan at u 6.47, v 13.37, on the south wall's line, so the two pictures show one stack, raised by the remodel past its mansard. Built there on the cornice (chimneys.stacks, u 6.5, v 13.2, 1.2 by 0.75 m, panelled and capped as the north stacks are), and the stack T-2465 had stood over the wing on the engraving's ray alone (u 10.2, v 11.2) retired. Through this camera its shaft rises behind the eave at x 251-321 px against the photograph's 245-345 (the cap's spread to 251-345); its top, at 15.85 m where the engraving draws it, stands over the frame, where the photograph's cap (y 30 px, about 14.2 m) is the stack before the remodel raised it, which this photograph predates as it predates the mansard

Its brackets are too dark here to count, and this photograph cannot measure the eave's height (the camera's solve: the band's height sets it, and the fence hides the ground), so the engraving's storey-line item, open in its own record, stays the place the eave's height is argued
